post.caption: Boomers are 1 in 5 Americans but hold half the wealth. Millennials and Gen Z hold the debt. Here's why the gap keeps growing.

headline.text: Boomers own half of America's wealth.

say: Baby Boomers are about one in five Americans,
but they own half of all the wealth in the country.
Millennials and Gen Z, meanwhile, hold most of the debt.
In March I wrote about the great generational wealth divide.
Here's who owns what, why it happened, and what fixes it.

scenes.title: Boomers' share of America
scenes.source: Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts · U.S. Census Bureau
say: Boomers are about twenty-one percent of the population.
They hold fifty-one percent of the wealth.

scenes.title: Every $100 of U.S. household wealth
say: Out of every hundred dollars of household wealth,
Boomers hold fifty-one. Millennials hold about ten.

scenes.title: Share of wealth at the same age
scenes.subtitle: average age ~35
say: And this isn't just about age.
At the same age, Boomers owned twice the share Millennials own now.

scenes.title: Why it's harder to build wealth
say: a higher cost of living and slow wage growth all stack up.
And as that wealth gets passed down,
the gap won't close on its own. It gets inherited.
The full breakdown, and what fixes it, is on American Inequality.
